newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end mixed, insurance share jumps.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end mixed, insurance share jumps.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended mixed in trading that saw shares in the country's two largest banks drop sharply while Colombia's top insurer posted impressive gains.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.58 percent at 17,292.29 on above-average trading volume of nearly 9 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB slipped a barely noticeable 0.04 percent, meanwhile, closing at 1,129.62 on volume of about 2.3 billion pesos.
The day's movers were led by insurance giant Suramericana de Seguros, flagship of the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno industrial group.

Brokers said Suramericana, which accounted for more than 2.6 billion of volume in Medellin, closed up 4.11 percent on that city's exchange at an all-time high of 26,340 pesos per share on active buying by foreign funds and local investors alike.

"Foreign funds may even have sold to other funds at very high prices," one Bogota-based broker said the stock's sharp run-up. "It can't be ruled out that some partners in the company cut loose some of their stock to take advantage of the high valuations," he added.
He and others said it was too soon to say whether the move was purely speculative or the product of long-term investment.

Other winners included brewer Bavaria, which eked out a 0.41 gain to close at 8,080 pesos a share in Bogota despite ING Barings' annoucement that it was cutting the stock from buy to hold because it saw little upside following its recent rally. The stock has outperformed the market by 53 percent in dollar terms so far this year.

Losers on profit-taking were led by blue-chip Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary stock fell 3.04 percent in Bogota to end at 350 pesos per share. Banco de Colombia, the country's second largest bank after Ganadero, fell 2.85 percent in Bogota to 409 pesos per share, its lowest trading level this year.
